_comment: Cost of the one-shot form-finding stage, per geometry. Measured on the timing machine of Section 6.5.1 (Xeon Gold 5412U). Timings are the Elapsed line each fofin_*.py prints, which brackets scipy.optimize.minimize only and excludes I/O and plotting. ms_per_iter is one L-BFGS-B iteration: an equilibrium solve plus a gradient. The B5 and C5 entries carry a 'before' block recording the same script before the adjoint gradient and vectorised inflate were ported into it from fofin_D5.py; those runs were executed concurrently on separate cores, the rest with the machine otherwise idle.

B5 (6.4.2).note: stops at the iteration cap, not at convergence, so the wall clock is a floor in both states. Runs on input/B5.obj, a coarser mesh than the 497/929 remesh the inverse problem of 6.4.2 uses.

C5 (6.4.3).note: runs on data/C5/C5_remeshed.obj, the same file the inverse problem of 6.4.3 uses; compas welds it to 1114 vertices where the FEM driver reads 1309.

2part (6.4.1).optimiser: hand-coded gradient descent, 10 fixed steps, time_step 1.0
2part (6.4.1).harness: timed by scratchpad/time_crease_fdm.py, which reproduces the arithmetic of fofin_butt_steps.py with fd_numpy taken from compas_fd and the viewer calls dropped; the committed script imports compas.numerical and compas_view2 and cannot run here.
2part (6.4.1).note: 10 fixed steps with no convergence test - the deviation was still falling at step 10. The committed script also has a shape bug: qpre (a list of length n_e) plus sum_gradient (n_e, 1) broadcasts to n_e by n_e and assigns a whole row as each edge's force density, which fd_numpy then rejects; the harness applies the elementwise update the surrounding code implies. As committed the script therefore cannot have produced the stored mesh_out_2parts_*.json.

port_verification.note: adjoint against direct sensitivity at a perturbed q, and vectorised vertex normals/areas against compas vertex_normal()*vertex_area(), both on the meshes used.
